opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features — by far the biggest running cost. Includes $127.058M of stock-based compensation.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to engineering and security teams at large companies. Includes $43.442M of stock-based compensation.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day. Includes $26.629M of stock-based compensation.

follow100Note: The striking thing: R&D alone eats about $44 of every $100 — more than four times the operating profit it leaves behind. Datadog's GAAP profit is thin because stock-based pay ($205M in the quarter) runs through those same lines; on management's preferred non-GAAP basis the operating margin was 24%, not 1%. Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
otherDetail: Interest income and other income of $46.714M, less $2.6M of interest expense — net $44.114M.

segments.name: Platform subscriptions
segments.note: One integrated platform — monitoring, security and AI observability, priced per host and per feature. Datadog reports a single revenue stream.

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 29% to $953M, and the customers that matter most keep spending more: 603 customers now pay $1M+ a year, up 31% from 462 a year ago.
takeaways.title: Growth held at 29% into year-end

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $291M — 31 cents of every revenue dollar — while GAAP operating income was just $9M. The gap is mostly stock-based pay ($205M), which costs no cash.
takeaways.title: A cash machine underneath a thin GAAP profit

takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin was 1%; non-GAAP was 24% after adding back stock pay and amortization. The full year tells the same story: a $44M GAAP operating loss vs $768M non-GAAP.
takeaways.title: Two margins, one gap

verdict: Revenue grew 29% to $953 million and Datadog stayed profitable on a GAAP basis, but the GAAP operating margin was just 1% — stock-based pay is the wedge between the $9 million GAAP operating profit and $230 million non-GAAP.
